analysis.title: $64 Billion Of Quiet Selling: Goldman Shows Asset Managers Dumping S&P Futs Into Soft-Data Rally
key_insights: Goldman's Robert Quinn (Oct 3 note) says CFTC Commitment of Traders data through Sep 29 shows continued Non-Dealer S&P 500 futures selling, led by Asset Managers.
Non-Dealers sold $10.5bn in the week of Sep 22-29, the 5th week of selling in the past 6 since Aug 18, for a net -$63.7bn over that stretch.
Shorts dominated the latest week, but long unwinds were more than 70% of the selling across the full 1.5-month window.
Latest week by category: Asset Manager sold $11.7bn, Other sold $1.1bn, Hedge Fund bought $620mm, Non-Reportable bought $1.6bn.

Asset Manager liquidation of $5.5bn coincided with a 25bp jump in US 10Y real yields, and the rolling 3-month correlation between AM gross longs and USGGT10Y turned well into negative territory. Proximity to quarter-end suggested reallocation may have started early.
Below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a Nonfarm payrolls miss reduced October hike pricing and supported a 0.70% S&P recovery.
The December Adjusted Interest Rate future (Quinn's funding proxy) cheapened about 5bps, meaning deferred real rates rose marginally, so Quinn says S&P futures flows arguably remained bearish.
As of Sep 29, before additional probable sales, Asset Manager net length was at a 77% 2-year rank. Quinn expects ongoing challenges until yields convincingly reverse.
Goldman rates research sees a clearer skew toward lower yields, despite upward pressure from oil and resilient AI investment plans. Quinn treats this as the potential end to the futures selling.

Cullen Morgan's US VOL COLOR (Oct 3) flags a rapid decline in conviction and sentiment with SPX less than 1% from highs and Nasdaq at new highs. The Monetary Policy Optimism factor is at -8, record-low territory.
PB US L/S net leverage fell 2.2 points to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 Liberation Day and the 2nd percentile.
Morgan sees QQQ upside into earnings as priced too low, a vol/skew call that does not dispute the futures overhang.
Zero Hedge's view is to side with Quinn and treat the soft-data bounce as a hike-odds repricing, not evidence the futures selling is done.

tension_points.theme: S&P futures selling vs soft-data bounce
tension_points.bull_case: Soft PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a payrolls miss cut October hike odds and gave the S&P a 0.70% bounce, with Nasdaq at new highs and SPX within 1% of highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Non-dealers sold $63.7bn of S&P futures since Aug 18, Asset Manager net length is at a 77% 2-year rank, and the December Adjusted Interest Rate future cheapened about 5bps, so futures flows remain arguably bearish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields convincingly reversing lower would stop the futures selling, per Quinn.

theme_stances.key_argument: Soft data cut hike odds but did not clear the Asset Manager futures overhang, which needs yields to reverse convincingly.
theme_stances.evidence: expect ongoing challenges until yields convincingly reverse
